messages:
Maria: Quick question — customers running IPv6-only VPCs for edge devices are hitting us when we expect IPv4 control plane endpoints. Options brainstorm: dual-stack private endpoint, NAT64 on their side, or a Redwood relay that does translation. Thoughts?

Ryan: +1 we hit this in one PoC. Dual-stack is clean but brings cert + endpoint provisioning complexity for private endpoints.

Jana: NAT64 depends on customer ops; many orgs won't want to manage it. And it breaks client source preservation and complicates IP-based allowlists.

Michael: Relay/translation inside our VPC sounds operationally heavier (more egress, more public exposure). But we can centralize certs and metrics.

Maria: Key nonfunctional constraints: preserve client IP for rate-limiting, keep MTU sensible for attachments (we saw fragmentation with gre tunnels earlier), and minimize config customers must do.

Ryan: MTU hit: if we do a relay with encapsulation (IP-in-IP) we lose ~20 bytes, with GRE more. On large payloads (embeddings/kv sync), fragmentation increases p50 latency.

Jana: Could we advertise PMTU and clamp MSS on the proxy? Example iptables snippet we used before:
```
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
That helped in a previous transit-gw setup.

Michael: For certs, dual-stack means issuing subjectAltNames for both v4/v6 IPs or using DNS-based names. Private endpoints prefer fixed IPs — doing DNS + private resolver is extra ops.

Maria: Proposal A: default to presenting a dual-stack private endpoint where we control DNS entries; customers with IPv4-only or dual-stack are fine. For IPv6-only customers we fall back to a regional relay in their region that does 1:1 translation and preserves source via X-Forwarded-For plus optional TCP proxy protocol for infra customers.

Ryan: Fallback relay + proxy-proto is pragmatic. We still need to solve MTU: enforce MSS clamp at relay and document expected MTU (1400 default) to customers.

Jana: Ops concern: relay capacity/scale and SLO cost. Will need autoscaling with GPU pools? Not necessarily GPUs — it's just TCP proxy/trans. But still needs sizing.

Maria: Action items:
- Jana: estimate relay capacity and cost for regional peering (ETA 2d)
- Ryan: validate MSS clamp + pmtu across transit-gw and privatelink paths (ETA 1d)
- Michael: scope certs/dns changes for dual-stack private endpoints (ETA 3d)

infra-bot: Deploy check: created ticket NET-1489 to track relay infra work.

Jana: ping if you want a heatmap of IPv6-only customer regions — I can pull from onboarding logs.

Maria: Thanks — we'll pick this up in next architecture sync. :thumbsup:
